title: SSE granular snapshot handoff and toolcall quarantine for safe reconnects
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Clients reconnecting to SSE streams can cause partial or duplicated logical outputs when structured tool/function calls are emitted in-flight. Current resume tokens and chunk replay protect text continuity but do not guarantee single-execution semantics for side-effecting toolcalls. This ticket proposes adding a granular snapshot handoff protocol plus a quarantine window for toolcall execution to ensure idempotent and safe reconnection behavior across hosted and dedicated environments.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can reconnect and resume stream content without causing duplicate side-effecting toolcall invocations
Server emits a compact per-session snapshot marker that encodes last-committed output boundaries and outstanding quarantined toolcalls
Quarantined toolcalls are only executed once the session commit confirmation handshake completes or after a configurable TTL with audit logging
No measurable latency regression (>5ms P50) for non-toolcall token streaming paths in single-region hosted API
E2E tests covering mid-stream toolcall, disconnect, resume, and replay scenarios exist and run in CI
design_decisions: Introduce a small snapshot envelope (SnapshotMarker) sent periodically and immediately after any toolcall emission; SnapshotMarker is monotonic and contains: lastCommittableChunkId, quarantinedToolcallIds, sessionEpoch

Quarantine semantics: upon emitting a toolcall chunk the runtime places the call in a quarantined state where execution is deferred locally until the SnapshotMarker confirming the chunk is acknowledged by downstream resume-token or client ACK

On reconnect, client provides last-seen SnapshotMarker. Server computes delta: toolcalls in quarantine that were not confirmed will not be auto-executed; server will either re-send toolcall payloads for explicit client re-ack or mark as expired after TTL

Toolcalls must be executed idempotently at the provider integration layer; runtime will attach a deterministic invocation-id combining session, chunk id, and toolcall-id to enforce idempotency at downstream adapters

Backward compatibility: if client does not understand SnapshotMarker, server falls back to current resume-token model but does not guarantee single-execution semantics; this is explicitly documented as a compatibility trade-off
SnapshotMarker kept intentionally small to avoid increasing payload size and to allow passthrough across proxies and CDNs
implementation_plan: Runtime: add SnapshotMarker generation in stream assembler (emit after toolcall chunks and every X seconds where X default 2s)
Runtime: implement local quarantine store for in-flight toolcalls with TTL and persistence across short-lived process restarts (ephemeral in-memory plus durable checkpoint for Dedicated)
API: extend SSE event envelope with event-type: snapshot-marker and a compact JSON payload; update server TLS/headers to allow event-type passthrough
Client SDKs: update JavaScript and Python SDKs to parse SnapshotMarker, send lastSeenSnapshot in Reconnect handshake, and expose toolcall-quarantine callbacks to application developers
Adapters: patch integrations (webhooks/third-party tools) to accept invocation-id header and reject duplicate invocations (best effort); provide shim that stores recent invocation-ids for 24h
Docs: publish compatibility notes and migration guide for customers relying on side-effecting toolcalls
Testing: add CI matrix cases for hosted and dedicated, including simulated network partitions and proxy-induced truncation
rollout_plan: Feature behind a runtime feature-flag default ON for new sessions but OFF for legacy API keys; enable gradual exposure via console toggles
Week 1: internal dogfood on dev clusters with high-volume simulated toolcalls and reconnects
Week 2-3: opt-in beta for customers on Dedicated and a small set of hosted tenants; collect metrics
Week 4: opt-out deprecation window, migrate SDK defaults, enable broadly after monitoring checks
Fallback: if SnapshotMarker parsing fails, runtime logs compatibility warning and falls back to resume-token behavior
tests: Integration: end-to-end flow where a toolcall is emitted, client disconnects before commit, reconnects and confirms the SnapshotMarker, and the toolcall executes exactly once
Chaos: randomized drop of last bytes of stream, intermediate proxy buffering, simulated clock skew between client and server
Load: ensure streaming P50/P95 token latencies unchanged for non-toolcall clients at target QPS
monitoring: New metrics: snapshot_marker_emitted_rate, quarantined_toolcall_count, quarantined_toolcall_expiry_rate, toolcall_duplicate_detected_count
Dashboards: per-tenant time series for quarantined_toolcall_count and duplicate_detected_count with error budget overlay
Alerts: high duplicate_detected_count (>0.1% of toolcalls over 5m) triggers PagerDuty and auto-toggle to conservative mode
Audit logs: each executed toolcall records invocation-id, session, snapshot marker id, and whether it was executed from quarantine or normal path
comments: 2025-02-15 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/streaming/snapshot-handoff - decided to prefer compact marker shape to avoid CDN interference.
2025-02-18 - Liam Chen: Prototype implemented for SnapshotMarker emit and local quarantine store. Observed 2ms median overhead on emission path in microbenchmarks.
2025-02-21 - Design Review (Priya Rao): Suggested explicit client API for 'replay-safe' acknowledgement; requested UX doc for client-side hooks to alert developers to quarantined calls.
2025-02-25 - Security (Omar Malik): Flagged that invocation-id construction must not leak PII; confirmed deterministic id should use truncated SHA256(session|chunk|toolcall) and salt per-tenant.

2025-02-28 - QA (Janelle Park): Added failing integration test for proxy truncation; root cause was event-type header stripping by older nginx. Plan: fall back to embedding marker in a benign 'comment' SSE event for compatibility.
2025-03-02 - Liam Chen: Updated runtime to emit fallback comment-encoded marker when event-type headers absent. Preparing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
